# Sirach Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_004_page_001.jpg

---

4:1 My child, do not deprive the poor of their living, and do not make the needy wait with empty eyes.

4:2 Do not grieve the hungry, nor anger the poor.

4:3 Do not add trouble to a heart that is bitter, nor delay giving to the one in need.

4:4 Do not reject the suppliant in his affliction, and do not turn away your face from the poor.

4:5 Do not avert your eye from the needy, and give no one reason to curse you.

4:6 For if he curses you in the bitterness of his soul, his maker will hear his prayer.

4:7 Make yourself beloved in the congregation; bow your head before a great man.

4:8 Incline your ear to the poor, and answer him with peaceful words with humility.

4:9 Deliver the wronged from the hand of the wrongdoer, and do not be fainthearted in rendering judgment.

4:10 Be like a father to orphans, and act as a husband to their mother; then you will be like a son of the Most High, and he will love you more than your mother loves you.

4:11 Wisdom exalts her children and gives help to those who seek her.

4:12 Whoever loves her loves life, and those who seek her early will be filled with joy.

4:13 Whoever holds her fast inherits glory, and the Lord blesses the place where she enters.

4:14 Those who serve her serve the Holy One; the Lord loves those who love her.

4:15 Whoever obeys her will judge the nations, and whoever gives heed to her will dwell securely.

4:16 If he trusts her, he will inherit her, and his descendants will be in possession of her.

4:17 For at first she will walk with him on tortuous paths; she will bring fear and cowardice upon him, and will torment him by her discipline until she trusts him, and she will test him with her ordinances.

4:18 Then she will come back to him on the straight path and will gladden him, and will reveal to him her secrets.

4:19 But if he goes astray, she will forsake him and hand him over to his downfall.

4:20 Watch for the right moment and keep yourself from evil, and do not be ashamed of your very self.

4:21 For there is a shame that leads to sin, and there is a shame that leads to glory and favor.

4:22 Do not show partiality to your own disadvantage, and do not be in awe of anyone to your downfall.

4:23 Do not refrain from speaking at the opportune time, and do not hide your wisdom.

4:24 For wisdom is known through speech, and instruction through the words of the tongue.

4:25 Do not speak against the truth, and be ashamed of the errors of your ignorance.

4:26 Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not strive against the current of a river.

4:27 Do not subject yourself to a foolish person, and do not show partiality to an influential man.

4:28 Strive even unto death for the truth, and the Lord God will fight for you.

4:29 Do not be reckless in your speech, nor slack and remiss in your actions.

4:30 Do not be like a lion in your home, and do not be suspicious of your servants.

4:31 Let not your hand be extended to receive but clenched when it is time to give.

---

*Translator's Note: Hebrew fragments (Cairo Genizah MS A) extant here. v.10 "son of the Most High" — Greek huios Hypsistou. The phrase is remarkable; Ben Sira applies divine son-language to the generous person. vv.11-19 form a distinct "Wisdom poem" with Wisdom personified as a disciplining mother-figure.*
